_metadata.description: Reconciliation, console, the seams held open for capabilities not yet justified, and the market-driven expansions added 2026-08-13 from the competitive scan (RCR/CAT/ATT/CUR).

requirements.title: Reconciliation surfaces both unmatched sides
requirements.description: Matching the journal against an authoritative statement reports entries present in one and not the other, in both directions. A one-directional check finds missing records but never spurious ones.

validation.notes: A seeded mismatch in each direction produces exactly one finding each.

requirements.title: Console covers every perceivable state
requirements.description: Journal, position, goals and adapter health each render loading, empty, partial, stale and error states. Money is never colour-only — an outflow carries a sign and a label — and every chart has a table equivalent.

validation.notes: Feature tests assert each state renders with its documented selector.
BAS case asserts figures use tabular numerals and that status carries text.

requirements.title: Valuation accounts separate holdings from transactions
requirements.description: An account kind whose value changes without a transaction — investments, crypto — plus a valuation event kind that restates it. The seam is cheap now; the portfolio experience is not, and is deliberately excluded.

validation.notes: A valuation event changes a holding's value without creating an income posting.

requirements.title: Adapters extract on a declared trigger
requirements.description: Adapters move to their own scenario when any of three conditions holds: a third live adapter lands, adapters need retry schedules and sync cursors independent of the journal's clock, or stored credentials need rotation. Until then the contract is the boundary and the code lives here. The trigger is recorded so the split is a decision rather than a drift.

validation.notes: Reviewed at each adapter addition; the extraction decision is recorded in docs/internal/DECISIONS.md.

requirements.title: Events may reference an acquisition lot
requirements.description: A posting may reference a cost-basis lot so per-unit margin is knowable for resale. Only the reference is in scope; inventory management belongs to whatever capability actually runs a resale loop, and none exists yet.

validation.notes: A lot reference round-trips and constrains nothing else about the posting.

requirements.title: An expected event is an event with a projected basis
requirements.description: A recurring or expected future event enters through the same contract as any other, carrying basis `projected`. Position may include or exclude projected events, and says which it did. Modelling forecasts as a separate concept would create a second kind of truth the honesty rules do not cover; making them ordinary events means every existing provenance guarantee applies to them unchanged.

validation.notes: A projected event never contributes to a balance reported as authoritative.
Position computed with and without projected events differs, and each response states which basis set it used.

requirements.title: Rules assign categories and never amounts
requirements.description: Declared rules match events at ingest and set a deductibility category. A rule may not create, alter, or infer an amount, a date, or an account. Any model-assisted categorisation is a proposal an operator accepts, recorded with basis `derived` and the rule or model that produced it — never a silent write.

validation.notes: A rule that attempts to write an amount is rejected at declaration time.
An accepted model suggestion records basis `derived` and its producing model.

requirements.title: An event may carry evidence
requirements.description: A receipt or statement document may be attached to an event as the evidence layer under the categorised export. Attachment bytes are treated as sensitive and are covered by the same non-regenerable backup policy as the journal, because a categorised export without its evidence is materially less useful to an accountant.

validation.notes: An attachment round-trips and is reachable only through its owning event.
The export includes attachment references for every event that has one.

requirements.title: Currencies are reported separately and never converted
requirements.description: Balances, statements and position report each currency on its own line. No total spans two currencies and no rate is ever applied — the no-FX-engine guardrail in the PRD stands. A converted total would be a derived figure whose basis depends on a rate and a date the scenario does not own, which is exactly the kind of silently-wrong number the product exists to refuse.

validation.notes: A book holding two currencies produces two reported lines and no combined total.
